entity.summary: Sovereign layer-one decentralized derivatives exchange using a fully on-chain central limit order book, on-chain matching and settlement, cross-margin controls, and dedicated low-latency trading infrastructure. AFX launched its mainnet in May 2026 and suffered a major compromise of its operated custody bridge in July 2026 while remaining an active exchange record.
entity.notes: HEI consolidates the AFX sovereign chain, perpetual exchange, trading application, vault, explorer, and documentation surfaces into one exchange entity. AFX announced its sovereign L1 mainnet as live on May 18, 2026. On July 22, 2026, an attacker compromised AFX-operated infrastructure and validator signing capacity, causing the AFX-operated custody bridge to release approximately 24.15 million USDC. AFX later published a detailed post-mortem describing a software-supply-chain intrusion and platform-wide suspension of bridge operations during containment. The incident affected AFX-operated infrastructure rather than the native Arbitrum bridge and does not by itself establish a terminal exchange status. The first-party trading surface remained publicly available at the 2026-08-17 review.

events.title: AFX sovereign L1 mainnet launched
events.description: AFX announced that its sovereign Layer 1 mainnet for decentralized derivatives was live and opened the trading venue at app.afx.xyz/trade.
events.notes: The May 18 issuer announcement states that AFX Mainnet was live. A June 18 issuer update independently described approximately 36 days of mainnet operation, corroborating the mid-May launch window.

events.title: AFX-operated custody bridge was drained after validator infrastructure compromise
events.description: AFX reported a targeted software-supply-chain intrusion that progressed through internal infrastructure to a subset of DEX validators. Compromised validators co-signed a bridge call that transferred assets from the AFX-operated custody bridge; independent reporting measured the drain at approximately 24.15 million USDC. AFX suspended bridge-related operations and isolated the affected validator cluster during containment.
events.notes: The incident was confined to AFX-operated infrastructure; AFX and independent reporting state that the native Arbitrum bridge was not compromised. HEI records the temporary service effect as limited rather than inferring a terminal status.

evidence.title: AFX sovereign on-chain trading platform
evidence.notes: Current first-party trading surface describes AFX as a sovereign layer-one decentralized derivatives venue with a fully on-chain central limit order book, on-chain execution and settlement, and dedicated risk-control infrastructure; it remained publicly available after the July bridge incident at the 2026-08-17 review.

evidence.title: AFX protocol trading metrics
evidence.notes: Independent protocol metrics report current non-zero perpetual volume, fees, revenue, open interest, TVL, and active addresses for AFX, corroborating active exchange operation.

evidence.title: AFX Launches Sovereign Layer 1, Providing an Optimized Execution Environment for On-chain Perp DEXes
evidence.notes: Issuer-supplied announcement states that AFX Mainnet was live and directs traders to the AFX trading application.

evidence.title: AFX Surpasses $710M Mainnet Volume, Launching 100x Leverage and Programmatic Flywheel to Align Sovereign L1 Ecosystem
evidence.notes: Issuer update reports more than $710 million of cumulative volume within 36 days of mainnet launch, corroborating the May 2026 launch timing and subsequent active operation.

evidence.title: A Detailed Post-Mortem on the AFX Security Incident
evidence.notes: First-party post-mortem describes the July 22 compromise path, validator compromise, transfer from the AFX-operated custody bridge, immediate suspension of bridge-related operations, containment, and subsequent infrastructure hardening.

evidence.title: Arbitrum-based AFX Trade drained of $24 million after bridge keys compromised
evidence.notes: Independent reporting corroborates the roughly 24.15 million USDC drain, compromised validator signing keys, movement of stolen funds, and that the native Arbitrum bridge was not affected.
